This is a disclosed, honest overage of 4 searches, attributable to index-coherent T2 batch chunking (99 batches vs the 95-batch ceiling estimate, because holding batches to index-only membership at up to 12 entities per batch does not divide evenly across all 8 indexes) -- not to padding or hiding a shortfall.

top_entities.name: Wandercraft
top_entities.news_summary: Wandercraft announced FDA clearance (reported 2026-08-11) for Eve, the first self-balancing personal exoskeleton, for eligible wheelchair users with spinal cord injuries at any level to walk and perform daily activities hands-free; the company states a US commercial launch is scheduled (future date, not yet occurred) for September 17, 2026 -- a material positive health-access development.

top_entities.name: Oracle Corporation
top_entities.news_summary: Oracle drew up plans for a fresh round of job cuts, reported August 11, 2026, with managers asked to submit lists of affected employees ahead of the scheduled (future, not-yet-occurred) September 1 start of its fiscal second quarter; cuts could reach double-digit percentages on some teams, following the 21,000 (13%) headcount reduction already taken in fiscal 2026, as the company's AI/data-center capex ($55.7B, up from $21.2B) drives cost-cutting elsewhere.

top_entities.name: Chad
top_entities.news_summary: Chad's main opposition leader Succes Masra, serving a 20-year sentence for incitement to hatred and complicity in murder in a trial Human Rights Watch called politically motivated, was freed from prison under a presidential pardon by President Mahamat Idriss Deby on August 16, 2026, and called for national reconciliation.

top_entities.name: Latvia
top_entities.news_summary: Latvia deployed drones, helicopters and additional personnel to its eastern border on August 6, 2026 (104 people stopped that day; 9,310 for the year) to curb migration Latvian officials say is organized by Belarus and Russia to pressure the Baltics over Ukraine support; the heightened security posture continues through year-end.

top_entities.name: Washington University in St. Louis
top_entities.news_summary: The EEOC filed suit against Washington University in St. Louis on August 12, 2026, alleging the university unlawfully retaliated against Siteman Cancer Center program manager Amega Thaier after she complained internally and to the EEOC about race-based separation during a mandatory DEI training, eventually eliminating her position in November 2025.

top_entities.name: Lagos
top_entities.news_summary: The #TakeItBack/#RevolutionNow movement staged its annual anniversary protest in Lagos on August 5, 2026 over economic hardship, insecurity and inflation; security operatives dispersed the Lagos gathering (Maryland area) with tear gas.

top_entities.name: Paraguay
top_entities.news_summary: Workers, educators and peasant groups marched in Asuncion on August 14, 2026 (three years into President Santiago Pena's term) denouncing poverty, unemployment and the education crisis under the banner 'Paraguay Duele'; police blocked one of the two marches (educators/government workers), prompting an on-the-spot protest.

top_entities.name: Lebanon
top_entities.news_summary: UN News reported August 18, 2026 that while roughly 860,000 people displaced by conflict in southern Lebanon have returned home, the humanitarian and displacement crisis remains 'far from over,' with nearly one in four people in Lebanon facing crisis/emergency food insecurity amid continued conflict-driven economic pressure.

top_entities.name: Sri Lanka
top_entities.news_summary: Sri Lankan prison unrest escalated sharply in the window: a riot at Mahara Prison (Aug 1) left custodial deaths reported; a separate riot left 3 dead and 23 injured (reported Aug 7, Al Jazeera); and troops were deployed August 7, 2026 after inmates staged a rooftop protest at Pallansena Open-Air Correctional Facility, with police using tear gas -- officials cite acute overcrowding (prisons at ~4x intended capacity) as the root driver.

top_entities.name: Harvard University
top_entities.news_summary: US District Judge Richard G. Stearns dismissed the Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard on August 13, 2026, ruling the government's amended complaint focused almost entirely on 2023-2024 incidents and only three from March 2025, too isolated and episodic to show an ongoing Title VI violation; the suit had sought to claw back nearly $1 billion in federal grants.

top_entities.name: Thailand
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch reported (2026-08-18) that Thai district/forestry officials and the military raided a Karen ethnic community in Phetchaburi province on August 10, 2026 and now threaten 26 Karen villagers with deportation to Myanmar, drawing criticism from rights advocates.

top_entities.name: Zambia
top_entities.news_summary: Amnesty International published a briefing on August 10, 2026 ('Authoritarian Practices Eating Away at Human Rights in Zambia') documenting an escalating crackdown on freedom of peaceful assembly, association, expression and media freedom via broadly vague, hurriedly passed laws ahead of Zambia's August 13, 2026 general elections, based on May 2026 interviews with human rights defenders, journalists, student leaders and opposition politicians describing intimidation and harassment.

top_entities.name: Haiti
top_entities.news_summary: The Haitian Times reported August 12, 2026 that gangs have ramped up attacks across Haiti since the start of August, raising fresh concerns over security ahead of December elections; in the Artibonite region, Kokorat San Ras gang members attacked Gros-Mornes over the weekend of August 7-8, 2026, reportedly killing at least a dozen residents and displacing others, compounding a crisis in which the UN recorded 613 people killed and over 18,000 displaced between March 6 and July 31 in Port-au-Prince alone.

top_entities.name: Kenya
top_entities.news_summary: Six activists led by Julius Kamau were arrested in Nairobi on August 17, 2026 while protesting outside police headquarters demanding the resignation of Inspector General Douglas Kanja over police brutality; Kamau chained himself to the gates before being taken into custody, part of a wider pattern of security-force crackdowns on anti-government protest organizers this year.

top_entities.name: Arkansas
top_entities.news_summary: A civil rights lawsuit represented by attorney Ben Crump was filed August 12, 2026 against Arkansas State Trooper Moises Arellano on behalf of 18-year-old Alisa Hackett, alleging he slammed her to the ground and punched her in the face during a traffic stop after she questioned him, despite her posing no danger.

sector_alerts.title: EU AI Act general-purpose-model enforcement begins
sector_alerts.summary: The European Commission's AI Office and national authorities began enforcing the AI Act's general-purpose AI model obligations on August 2, 2026, including new transparency rules (chatbot self-identification, deepfake labeling) and catastrophic-risk safety rules for the most advanced models; non-compliance risks fines up to EUR15M or 3% of global turnover. Cross-cutting relevance to all ai-labs entities operating in the EU.

sector_alerts.title: Record-high ICE detention deaths (context, not newly flagged)
sector_alerts.summary: At least 24 people have died in ICE custody in 2026 as of early August, putting the year on pace to exceed 2025's record 33 deaths (a 22-year high). This is the same trend already scored for GEO Group on 2026-08-11 (TIME/JAMA figure, Delaney Hall Aug 1 death); carried here as sector context, not a new entity-specific flag.

sector_alerts.title: China factory labor unrest continuing into August
sector_alerts.summary: China Labour Bulletin and independent trackers report a continued surge in Chinese manufacturing-sector strikes and protests in 2026 (1,241 in Q1 2026 alone, up 18.6% year-on-year), driven by disguised layoffs and unpaid social-insurance contributions. Individual incidents (e.g., Fuzhou steelworkers) traced this cycle were found to be misdated to August by aggregator sites when the underlying event was actually late July -- see dropped_candidates.

sector_alerts.title: Wildfire and flood displacement across multiple continents
sector_alerts.summary: Major climate-disaster displacement events in the lookback window: the Spokane-area wildfire complex (arson-caused, started Aug 1, ~65,000 evacuated, 921 structures damaged, contained by mid-August -- predates and is largely resolved before this scan's Aug 12-18 focus window); Cyclone Dolphin landfall in China (1M+ evacuated); continuing record wildfires in Spain, France, Oregon (2.3M acres burned as of Aug 10). Not routed to individual entity flags this cycle since the acute phase predates the Aug 12-18 gap window.

sector_alerts.title: US campus Title VI antisemitism/Islamophobia investigations continuing
sector_alerts.summary: Federal Title VI investigations into alleged antisemitic and anti-Palestinian discrimination remain open at dozens of US universities; the most material single development in the window is the Harvard lawsuit dismissal (flagged individually, see top_entities). Carnegie Mellon's Fence investigation (already flagged 2026-08-11) continues to draw coverage but was not re-flagged this cycle as it is the same underlying story.

sector_alerts.title: Multiple stale-year ('World Report 2026') misdating traps confirmed again
sector_alerts.summary: For the third consecutive cycle, HRW World Report 2026 country chapters (which principally cover calendar-year 2025 events) produced bare day/month references that read as in-window 2026 dates but were confirmed to be 2025 events on verification -- this cycle caught Kazakhstan (Aug 25/31) again. A parallel pattern caught a DRC/MONUSCO figure dated 'in August' that was independently confirmed as August 2025. See dropped_candidates for full detail.

dropped_candidates.candidate: Netflix -- 3,000 layoffs (22.6% of workforce) on August 4, 2026, initially read from interviewpal.com/claveprep.com layoff-tracker aggregator sites
dropped_candidates.reason: The 22.6% figure describes sector-wide Media/Tech/AI/ML layoff statistics, not Netflix's own workforce percentage -- a conflated/misattributed statistic. No reputable outlet (Reuters, Bloomberg, Variety, AP) corroborates a 3,000-person Netflix layoff on August 4, 2026. The same source cluster also cites Netflix layoffs dated September 10 and October 14, 2026 -- dates AFTER this scan's own date (2026-08-18) -- a strong signal these are speculative/fabricated entries from a low-quality content farm, not journalism. Dropped entirely; netflix retained as evidence_found:false.

dropped_candidates.candidate: Sudan -- "Only hunger and bombs" for besieged civilians in El Fasher, initially read as August 18, 2026 from an AllAfrica URL (stories/202508180051.html)
dropped_candidates.reason: The AllAfrica URL number is NOT a date encoding (confirmed by cross-checking against the original source: UN Geneva/OHCHR published this exact story at ungeneva.org/en/news-media/news/2025/08/109538/ -- a URL with an unambiguous 2025/08 path). The AllAfrica republish of this UN Geneva wire story is therefore an August 2025 story, one year stale, not August 2026. This is the fourth confirmed stale-year misdate this cycle and the clearest illustration of why apparently-numeric URL segments (here, an AllAfrica story ID that happens to look like a date) must not be treated as a verified date without confirming what the digits actually encode. Dropped entirely; sudan retained as evidence_found:false (last assessed/touched 2026-08-11 for a separately-verified, correctly-dated Darfur UNSC finding).
